title: Minimum Length of Anagram Concatenation
statement:
The string `s` was built by writing several anagrams of one hidden string `t` one after another (an anagram of `t` uses exactly the same letters as `t` with the same counts, in any order; `t` itself counts).

Return the smallest length `t` could have. Note that `t = s` always works, so an answer exists.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

If `t` has length `len`, then `s` splits into `n / len` consecutive pieces of length `len`, so `len` must divide `n = s.length`. A length works exactly when every piece has the same letter counts as the first piece. So try the divisors of `n` from smallest to largest and return the first that works; `len = n` always does.

## Approach

1. For each `len` from 1 to `n`, skip it unless it divides `n`.
2. Count the letters of the first piece `s[0..len)` into `first`.
3. For every later piece starting at `start`, count its letters into `count` and compare with `first`; stop as soon as one differs.
4. If every piece matched, return `len`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "abba"`, `n = 4`.

- `len = 1`: `first` is one `a`; the piece `"b"` differs, so `valid` becomes `false`.
- `len = 2`: `first` is one `a` and one `b`; the only other piece `"ba"` has the same counts, so `valid` stays `true` and the answer is `2`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n · d(n)), where d(n) is the number of divisors of `n` (at most 128 for n ≤ 10⁵): each candidate scans `s` once, plus 26 per piece for the comparison.
- Space: O(1): two arrays of 26 counts.

## Pitfalls

- Only lengths that divide `n` can work; a non-divisor would leave a partial piece.
- Dividing `n` by the gcd of the letter counts is tempting but wrong: `"aabb"` has counts 2 and 2, yet `"aa"` and `"bb"` are not anagrams, so the answer is 4.
- Compare full letter counts, not just the set of letters present.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | length of `s` |
| `len` | candidate length of `t` |
| `first` | letter counts of the first piece |
| `start` | index where the current piece begins |
| `count` | letter counts of the current piece |
| `valid` | whether every piece so far matched `first` |

narration.2: n is the length every candidate must divide.
narration.3: Try candidate lengths for t from smallest to largest.
narration.4: A length that does not divide n cannot split s into whole pieces.
narration.5: Prepare 26 letter counters for the first piece.
narration.7: Count each letter of the first piece s[0..len).
narration.9: Assume this length works until a piece disagrees.
narration.10: Visit each later piece, stopping early once one fails.
narration.11: Fresh counters for the current piece.
narration.13: Count each letter of the current piece.
narration.15: The piece is an anagram of the first only if all 26 counts match.
narration.17: Every piece matched, so this is the smallest valid length.
narration.19: Never reached in practice, since len = n always works.
